name: A Twisty Movement
description: A dragon symbolizes wisdom, power and wealth. On Lunar New Year's Day, people model a dragon with bamboo strips and clothes, raise them with rods, and hold the rods high and low to resemble a flying dragon. A performer holding the rod low is represented by a 1 , while one holding it high is represented by a 2 . Thus, the line of performers can be represented by a sequence a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . Little Tommy is among them. He would like to choose an interval [ l , r ] ( 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n ), then reverse a l , a l + 1 , ..., a r so that the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence of the new sequence is maximum. A non-decreasing subsequence is a sequence of indices p 1 , p 2 , ..., p k , such that p 1 < p 2 < ... < p k and a p 1 ≤ a p 2 ≤ ... ≤ a p k . The length of the subsequence is k .
input_specification: The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2000) , denoting the length of the original sequence. The second line contains n space-separated integers, describing the original sequence a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (1 ≤ a i ≤ 2, i = 1, 2, ..., n ) .
output_specification: Print a single integer, which means the maximum possible length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence of the new sequence.
subsubtopic: 461. Interval DP / Range DP / Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)
approach_summary: Iterate over interval length len from 1 to N and left endpoint l. Transition by splitting at midpoint k: dp[l][r] = min/max_k (dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r] + cost) in O(N^3).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 933A — A Twisty Movement [461. Interval DP / Range DP / Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)]
topic_editorial.summary: Interval / Range Dynamic Programming by interval length.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The problem satisfies interval substructure: the optimal cost for range $[l, r]$ depends on splitting into subsegments $[l, k]$ and $[k+1, r]$ for some pivot $k \in [l, r-1]$. Computing shorter intervals first ensures that all subproblems are ready when evaluating longer intervals.
